about: Answer views in a reply (ADR 264, #1623): a ```ui fence holds a JSON tree of the catalog's components (lib/ui-catalog.json); the apps read it with one generic validator driven by the catalog (public/answer-view.js, test/answer-view.test.js; the Android app reads the same cases in its own ticket). `cases`: `source` is what the fence holds (with `repeat`, its `mark` replaced by `with` written `times` times), then either `drawn`, the normalised view `{ alt, root }` with only what was read (defaults are the drawing's own, a value that was cut or left out is not there), or `refused`, why the fence is drawn as code, with `alt`, what could be read of the fence's alt for the quiet line above the code (an empty text without one). `problems` lists what was left out or cut and where (`at` is the node's path, `prop` the prop inside it), in the order it was met; a case without it has none. `replies`: a reply's Markdown (`done` is false while it is still being written, true when it has ended; true when not given) and `parts`, in order: `text` (Markdown between the fences), `view`, `code` (a fence drawn as code with its `alt` and why), and `drawing` (a fence still being written: the reply shows "Drawing a view…" and waits). `sends`: what a view posts as the owner's next message (ADR 265): `view` is a drawn tree, its nodes counted by `path` (the root is `0`, its children `0.0`, `0.1`, …); `values` holds what the owner changed, by the path of the input (a text, a number, a pair for a range, a list for a multi-select, or a boolean); `posts` is the form's message, or `presses` the message of each button by its path, and `shows` what is written on a button before it is pressed (what it sends, when that is not its label; ADR 265). A button's `send` or `label` that reads as one of the catalog's `reserved` phrases (lower case, only letters and digits compared) is not read: see the case of `cases` that names it. `countdowns` (wave 3): the time left to a countdown's `to` (a day, or a day and time with an optional Z or offset, else the owner's own zone, `offset` minutes east of UTC) at `now`, as the words a countdown shows (`shows`, in English: days and hours, hours and minutes, minutes and seconds, seconds; `over` once it has come; null where `to` can't be read as a real day and time). `calendars`: a calendar's `month` as its number of `days` and the weekday of its first (`start`, Monday 0), null where it is no month; `outlines`: the `depths` a tree's items were written at and the depths they are `shown` at; `shades`: how dark each cell of a heatmap is, 0 to 1 (an empty cell none). Paired lists: a list whose items stand by position with those of another (a comparison's `values` under its `options`, a table row's cells under its `columns`, a chart's points under its `labels`, a heatmap's cells under its rows and columns) never has an item shift its neighbours: where the catalog says `by`, an item left out of the one list is left out of the other at the same place; where it says `inPlace`, an item that can't be read is a blank in its place (an empty text, a null number, an empty row). A rule changes here and in every app together.

cases.name: a quiz whose answer follows its option when an earlier one is left out (a reserved phrase, an item that is no text), and has none when its own option, or a place past the list, is the one that is gone
a quiz is read by the place the bot counted: past the eighth option nothing is named, a rounded or written number is a place, and the last kept option is the answer when it is the one named
a comparison keeps its pick on the option it named when an option before it is left out, and drops the pick when the option itself is gone or the number is past the list
a table column that is left out takes its cell with it in every row, and a cell that is no text keeps its place as a blank
a comparison option that is left out takes its value with it in every row, and a value that is no text keeps its place as a blank
a chart keeps every label and every point where the bot put it: one it cannot read is a blank label or a gap, in every series
a heatmap keeps its cells under their row and column: a cell it cannot read stays empty, a row that is no list is an empty row, a label it cannot read is blank
a data component bound to a tile keeps its tile and its path, with the values it was written with (live numbers, #1630)
a chart and a table bound to a tile keep the path of each series, the field of each row and of each column
a tile and a path are texts, cut to their length; a component that does not bind has no use for them, and one that is not data drops them
